rationale: All test evaluations follow models trained and selected using training data, validation data, or cross-validation. No test metric is captured, compared, or used to choose a model, architecture, or hyperparameter. The reported preprocess_before_split finding is a false positive because preprocessing is fitted exclusively on training partitions and applied to validation/test partitions using transform only. The no_stratify findings concern a continuous-target regression split, where stratification is inappropriate.

The StandardScaler at cell 35 is fitted on the whole two-column frame but its output feeds only the from-scratch gradient-descent demo at cell 36 and the loss curve at cell 39; no test metric is computed from it. The evaluated path is cell 55, which splits the raw frame, cell 56, which fits LinearRegression on X_train only, and cell 62, which prints train and test MSE and R2. Cells 76 to 84 fit polynomial and log transforms on all rows but report only in-sample R2 for curve shape, and cell 92 re-splits before the forest demo at cell 93. An unused teaching block is not leakage, and the no_stratify findings concern a continuous regression target.

The high finding at cell 22 line 29 flags the max subtraction inside the softmax, which reduces along axis 1 and therefore acts within a single row; it cannot carry a dataset-level statistic. The real standardisation is cell 24 lines 12 to 15, which computes mean and std from X_train after the split at cell 24 line 9 and applies them to both X_train and X_test. The network is then trained on X_train and scored once on X_test at cell 24 lines 29 to 33, and no later cell re-splits or reuses the holdout.

Cell 90 splits off 20 percent with a fixed random_state and cell 91 fits and scores a linear model, so the first reported number comes from a clean holdout. Cell 96 then runs GridSearchCV with ShuffleSplit over the entire X and y, whose folds include the held-out rows, and cell 97 uses that table to choose the deployed algorithm. No test score is reported after the search and the exported model at cell 105 is the estimator fitted at cell 91, so no presented metric is provably contaminated, yet a model choice was made with the test rows participating. Execution counts are non-monotonic elsewhere in the file, but cell 91 runs at count 58 and cell 96 at count 60, so this ordering is not in doubt. The nominal location dummies at cell 81 are not fitted statistics.

Cell 39 one-hot encodes a four-level transaction type over the whole frame, which carries no target statistic; the split at cell 53 and the validation carve-out at cell 54 follow, and SMOTE at cell 56 is fitted on X_train only with the validation and test blocks untouched. Every model score in cells 64, 72, 82 and 87 comes from a model fitted on training rows and evaluated on X_test. The F1 at cell 13 scores an analyst rule against labels on the same rows; it is an in-sample rule check, not a model result, and the rule is never fitted. The out-of-order execution counts affect when cells ran, not what feeds what.

The sweep config at cell 9 maximizes a metric named accuracy, and cell 16 is the only place that metric is logged: accuracy_score on predictions computed from X_test. The swept parameters are booster, max_depth, learning_rate and subsample only, so seed 117 and test_size 0.33 keep their defaults and all 25 trials at cell 19 reuse the same test split. Hyperparameter selection is therefore performed directly on the reported test accuracy. The dossier is mistaken on one point: train_test_split does pass random_state=config.seed, which makes the reuse stronger rather than weaker. The notebook stores no execution counts, but the mechanism is explicit in the code.

Cell 1 line 6 fits SimpleImputer on the complete feature matrix and cell 2 splits the imputed result, so the column means seen by every training row were computed with the test rows included. The target one-hot at cell 1 line 5 is fine and the grid search at cell 5 is correctly fitted on x_train only, but it operates downstream of the contaminated matrix. The means carry no target information and a random forest is fairly insensitive to them, which limits the effect but not the mechanism. The loader lives in utility.py and is not in the cache, so the number of missing values cannot be checked statically.

Cell 1 loads features_3_sec.csv, whose rows are 3-second segments, and the stored output of cell 4 shows consecutive rows named blues.00000.0.wav and blues.00000.1.wav, so one recording contributes many rows. Cell 5 splits by row with train_test_split and no grouping, so segments of the same track land on both sides, and the KNN assessed at cell 9 can match a test segment to its own recording. Cell 4 also fits StandardScaler on the full frame before that split, and the second split at cell 5 line 5 re-draws the partition after SelectKBest was fitted on the first training block.

Cell 1 lines 90 to 92 fit a StandardScaler then a MinMaxScaler pipeline on the entire expression matrix, and cell 1 lines 108 to 109 fit a second MinMaxScaler on the same full frame, so the mean, standard deviation, minimum and maximum of every column include the rows each fold later holds out. Cell 8 line 4 then builds KFold with shuffle and line 11 splits those pre-scaled rows, fitting the Keras model on the train indices and validating on the test indices, and cell 10 line 4 repeats the design for the classification head over a separately full-frame scaled matrix. There is no holdout, so the printed mean R2, MSE, MAE and accuracy are the only reported estimates and every fold inherited statistics from its own validation rows. Scaling statistics are not target information, but the guide treats full-frame statistics that reach the fit as confirmed, and here they reach every fit.

Cell 19 lines 3 and 4 fit RFE with a RandomForestClassifier and n_features_to_select 10 on the whole training file, using Y_train, and only cell 22 line 1 splits that same file 70/30, so the label of each row that becomes the internal test block helped choose the ten kept columns. Cell 21 lines 1 to 3 also fit a StandardScaler on the full training file before that split. The contamination reaches every downstream score: cells 33, 43 and 50 all predict the 30 percent block with features selected using that block. Cell 48 then tunes 30 Optuna trials by scoring x_test at line 6, so the tree hyperparameters are chosen on the holdout they are reported on at cell 50 line 4. The external test file is only refitted at cell 21 line 3 and never scored, so that scaler output is unused.

Cell 15 line 1 draws the minority spam class with replacement up to the majority count and line 2 concatenates those copies with the majority class, so the pooled frame contains many exact duplicate messages. Cell 24 line 3 then splits that pooled frame 70/30 and cell 27 reports accuracy on the held-out block, which almost certainly contains copies of messages the classifier trained on; cell 31 line 7 repeats the same error with a 90/10 split. Cell 32 line 1 compounds it by cross-validating over a TF-IDF matrix whose vocabulary and IDF weights were fitted on every row of that matrix at cell 31 line 19, so each fold validation rows shaped its own features. The first section at cells 17 to 20 is correctly ordered, but the balanced-versus-unbalanced comparison the notebook is built around is inflated by duplicated rows.

Cell 32 lines 2 and 3 fit PCA with 20 components on every preprocessed sample and line 8 calls decode on the reduced matrix, so the component basis was learned from the same runs that the cross-validated folds hold out and each held-out run contributed its voxel variance to the features used to decode it. Cell 17 lines 3 and 4 fit the same PCA for the plotting section, and cell 31 line 9 runs the helper on the raw voxels as a baseline. Cell 37 lines 4 and 5 name the problem as double dipping when feature selection is applied before the division into training and test sets, and cell 39 lines 3 to 10 demonstrate the correct Pipeline with PredefinedSplit over run ids. PCA is unsupervised, so no label crosses a fold boundary, but the printed baseline and PCA accuracies come from a contaminated design and cell 33 interprets them as a performance result.

Every medium fit_on_full_data finding names X_t or X_train, which are training partitions created at cells 43 and 45 rather than the whole frame. Cell 84 lines 9 to 13 fit StandardScaler on X_t and call transform on X_val, cell 94 lines 13 to 25 fit a fresh MinMaxScaler on each training fold and transform the validation fold, and cell 102 lines 1 to 8 fit on X_train and transform X_test for the final reported score. The iris block around cells 17 to 31 does fit on the whole toy frame, but it draws a decision boundary and reports no held-out score. The scaler discipline is correct everywhere a score is produced, so the findings are lookalikes.

Cell 10 line 1 fills Age with the median of every training row and cell 12 line 1 fills Embarked the same way, both before cell 14 line 2 splits that frame into trainData and valData, so the validation rows contributed to the statistics their own features were filled with. Cell 15 fits a depth 3 decision tree on trainData and cell 17 line 1 prints its accuracy on valData, the only score the notebook reports. The effect is bounded by roughly 177 missing ages and an untuned model, but the order is wrong and the reported accuracy is optimistic. The external Kaggle test file is never scored locally, so nothing re-enters from the submission. A separate defect at cells 6 and 19 maps train Sex male to 1 while mapping the test file male to 0, which is a submission bug rather than a leakage mechanism.

The five cell snippet fits nothing and splits nothing. Cell 1 line 2 imports cross_val_score from the removed sklearn.cross_validation module and cells 2 and 3 use Python 2 print statements, so the stored code cannot run on any current interpreter. There is no fitted transform, no holdout and no reused block to judge, and the review guide treats non-executable code as uncertain rather than legitimate because absence of evidence is not evidence of absence. Its intent is the textbook minimal cross-validation example on bundled datasets, which would be legitimate if it ran.

Cell 7 line 6 splits the bundled iris frame before any fit, cell 11 line 3 fits the multilayer perceptron on X_train only, and the partial_fit loop at cell 13 line 12 trains on X_train while computing log_loss on X_test purely to draw a 500 iteration learning curve, with no model selected from it. The PCA exercise cells 15 to 24 are empty templates and the k-means block at cell 33 line 14 is unsupervised clustering of iris for a scatter plot. The only findings are missing random_state and stratify, which are reproducibility notes rather than leakage. The test loss curve would become a concern only if an iteration count or model were chosen from it.

Cell 32 line 1 splits the encoded images 80/20 into train and test. Cell 53 line 12 fits the augmentation generator on the training block only, which is correct, but cell 59 lines 1 to 3 register EarlyStopping on val_loss with patience 5 and pass the callbacks list to fit_generator at lines 11 to 13 with validation_data=(X_test,y_test) for 400 epochs, so the epoch at which training stops is chosen by the test block. Cell 69 lines 1 to 3 then predict that same block and cell 75 line 1 reports accuracy_score on it, and the markdown heading at cell 74 calls it the validation set. The early-stopped model is the model whose accuracy is reported, and there is no second untouched block, so the printed score is selection-biased.

The artifact is a single code cell of 39 import statements. It reads no data, splits nothing, transforms nothing and fits nothing, and its stored outputs are a tqdm warning followed by an error, so the block did not even finish importing. No leakage mechanism can be located in the code that exists and there is no pipeline to adjudicate, so the guide places the artifact at uncertain rather than legitimate. Recording uncertain marks the candidate as handled so the batch selector does not offer it again.

Cell 2 lines 16 to 24 log and normalise the full frame, and the target SalePrice_log is still inside the frame when that happens, but no split, fit or score follows anywhere. Cells 4, 8, 13 to 15, 17 and 24 contain only the instruction comment, cell 21 lines 1 to 6 return an unassigned folds list, and cell 26 lines 7 to 10 set every partition to None. A full-frame transform that never reaches a fit cannot leak, and a template that cannot run cannot be judged legitimate, so the guide places this at uncertain. The missing answers, not the visible code, decide the verdict.

Cell 36 lines 5 to 12 hold out the last 20 percent of every road-segment series as test_data, and cell 37 line 1 with cell 38 line 1 build X and y from the remainder and test2 from that holdout. Cell 44 lines 31 to 38 fit each candidate model on X and y and compute SMAPE against test_data, cell 45 line 1 sorts the models by that SMAPE, and cells 47 and 48 minimise the same test_data SMAPE over 500 hyperopt trials, with fmin at cell 47 line 63. Cell 55 prints the chosen values, cell 56 refits on X and y and cell 57 line 1 reports SMAPE on the identical test_data block, so the reported number belongs to the block that chose both the model and its hyperparameters. Cell 65 lines 46 to 68 then hard-code those same values into the models function, so the tuned result is what the submission pipeline carries. The sine and cosine FunctionTransformer at cell 26 lines 2 to 6 is stateless, so that scanner finding is a false positive.

Cell 3 lines 15 to 17 put every non-object column with enough distinct values in num_cols, so Salary is inside df[cat_cols+num_cols] at cell 13 line 3. Cell 13 lines 5 and 6 MinMax-scale that frame, cell 14 lines 2 to 5 run KNNImputer with 5 neighbours over every row and invert the scaling, and cell 15 line 1 stores the result as Salary_Imputed_Knn. Cell 23 lines 2 to 4 then make that column the target and split only afterwards. Every missing salary was therefore reconstructed from the other columns of the whole frame, including rows that later form the test block, and the model is fitted and scored on a target that its own features produced. The filled column is the label rather than a feature statistic, so this is target leakage as well as full-frame preprocessing, and cell 35 scaling individual columns later does not change it.

Cell 12 line 1 appends the Kaggle test frame to the train frame, cells 19 and 22 fill missing Age and Fare with the mean of that combined frame, and only cell 31 lines 1 to 2 and cell 37 line 2 separate the partitions and draw the split. The test passengers therefore contributed to the two fill values that every training row received. The StandardScaler at cell 40 lines 3 and 4 is fitted on X_train and applied to X_test, so scaling is correct and is not the mechanism. The effect is bounded because only the missing values are filled, but the guide confirms any full-frame statistic that reaches the fit or the score.

Cell 2 lines 8 to 10 convert the date column and sort the frame by date, and cell 49 lines 4 to 7 then call train_test_split with a 20 percent test size and no shuffle=False, so a daily dam-occupancy series is split at random across the whole calendar and most test days have immediate neighbours in the training block. Cell 60 lines 9 to 16 grid-search the voting weights on that split and report MSE and RMSE, and cell 62 lines 1 to 7 repeat the same random split. The series is strongly autocorrelated and the notebook builds no lagged or rolling features, so the only protection against look-ahead was the ordering, and the split discarded it.

Cell 10 line 3 drops the label and the four class-probability columns before X_full is built, line 7 splits 90/10 into train and validation, and lines 13 to 15 fill with medians taken from X_train and apply the same values to validation and test. Cell 11 lines 5 and 6 oversample the training block only, cell 12 lines 7 to 9 fit KNNImputer on X_train and transform the other blocks, and cell 14 lines 9 to 11 fit StandardScaler on X_train and transform the other blocks. Cell 15 tunes with 5-fold CV inside X_train_norm and cell 16 lines 3 to 13 score the untouched validation block, so holdout rows never reach a fit. The commented filtering and encoding blocks are inert and the class-probability columns were excluded from X, so the low scanner signal is a lookalike.

Cell 17 line 1 splits 70/30 into X_train1 and X_test1. Cell 21 lines 8 to 14 fit IterativeImputer on X_train1 and transform both blocks, and cell 27 lines 5 to 8 fit StandardScaler on X_train1 and transform both. Cells 29 and 30 use the holdout for a dummy baseline, and then cell 31 lines 1 to 3 concatenate the two already transformed blocks back into X_kcv and y_kcv of 1309 rows. Cell 32 lines 4 to 7 and cell 33 lines 20 to 24 run 10-fold cross_val_score over that union with no Pipeline, so the transform is never refit inside a fold and about 70 percent of each validation block consists of rows that had contributed to the imputer and scaler which produced their own features. The AUC table is the last computation in the notebook and is its model comparison, and no untouched test set remains, so the only reported estimate is the contaminated one.

Cell 8 lines 1 and 2 copy the gender_submission labels onto the Kaggle test rows and append that frame to the train frame. Cell 49 line 1 computes the Age mean over the combined frame and fills with it, cell 50 does the same for Fare, and cells 59 to 63 fit a linear regression for Age on every row with a known age from both partitions and then predict the missing ages on both sides. Cell 80 lines 1 and 2 split the assembled frame back into the original train and test rows for the final fit at cell 81, so training rows with a missing age carry values learned from test rows and test features were partly produced by a model trained on other test rows. The final evaluation at cell 81 is also scored against submission labels rather than ground truth, which is a separate validity defect.
